records.name: Hernand
records.summary: Temperate western duchy of grassland, forest and river valleys, ruled by House Celeste from the City of Hernand.
records.body: Hernand occupies the west and southwest of Pywel: rolling grassland and farmland cut by river valleys, with forest, mountain and a stretch of coast. House Celeste is the ducal house, descended from the knight Canta; House Serkis runs internal affairs as the marquis house, with Houses Alfonso, Felix, Grace and Roberts beneath them. [[place:hernand-castle]] is the capital and stronghold. The prologue and Chapters 1-6 play here (Chapter 5 also steps into Demeniss; Chapter 6 is set in [[region:calphadean-territory]]), and Hernand returns as a secondary setting in Chapters 7-8 and the epilogue.

records.name: Pailune
records.summary: Snowbound northern mountains held by tribes and militias, with no single ruler and the settlement of Pailune as its hub.
records.body: Pailune is Pywel's coldest country: steep, snow-covered mountains in the north with poor visibility. No house rules it by the time of the story; the Pailune Militia around [[place:pailune]] and the Beighen, Knytlingar, Longleaf, Skoghorn and Stjar tribes hold ground, while the [[faction:black-bears]] and Lonely Jackals occupy stretches of it. The [[faction:greymanes]] began here as its protectors under founder Gian, and a Beighen resistance known as the Blue Fangs fights the occupation. Chapter 7 (Homecoming) is the main-story chapter, shared with Demeniss; Chapter 8 uses Pailune again as a secondary setting, and the region's fast-travel bell opens only after Chapter 7.

records.name: Demeniss
records.summary: Cliff-walled plains of fortresses and noble courts, left unstable by House Thorel's vacant throne.
records.body: Demeniss sits on golden plains behind high walls: fortified cities and large military works on a cliff line. House Thorel once unified its territories, but King Edward Thorel lies in a coma with no named heir; Houses Azerian, Byron, Elemore, Marshell (patron of Grand General Bastier) and Wells (said to govern the south) contest the vacuum, and [[character:gabriel-caliburn]] seizes power during Blood Coronation. [[place:demeniss-castle]] is the political capital; sources disagree on whether the city or the castle is the preferred name. Chapters 8, 10 and 12 are its main-story chapters; it also appears in Chapters 5, 7 and 9 and in the epilogue.

records.name: Delesyia
records.summary: Pywel's machine-age region, run by engineering guilds rather than a noble house, and the setting of Chapter 11.
records.body: Delesyia is the most mechanically distinct part of Pywel: factories, railways, automated works and airships, while Hernand and Demeniss stay medieval. No ruling noble house is named; [[character:marni]] and the institutions around him (Society of Progress, Delesyia National Institute, Delesyian Aerial Force, Cogknights, Marni's Tinkertons) are the civil power, with the Ironwheel of Dewhaven arguing that machines should only assist people. The Ironflame Orcs under [[character:valgash]] hold [[region:gorthak]], and the Wyvernflames occupy Fort Windridge. Chapter 11 (Truth and Reality) is the main-story chapter; no source read here names a clear capital, though [[place:delesyia-castle]] and Marni's clocktower (the Toll of Delesyia bell) are the closest hubs.

records.name: Crimson Desert
records.summary: Lawless red-sand country in the north-east, with Varnia as its religious and trade hub and no sovereign house.
records.body: The Crimson Desert is the north-easternmost major region: red sand, canyons, oases and sandstorms, with pockets of wetland and rainforest. No nation rules it; settlements, pilgrim towns, merchant guilds, tribes and outlaw bands share the ground. Civil names include the Lords of Unclaimed Lands, the Arcosa Tribe, the Redwind Merchant Guild, the pilgrim village of [[place:urdavah]] and the holy city Varnia (worship of Atima), plus the Sage of the Desert; hostile names include the Sandfang Marauders, Goldenscale Bandits, Dusksong, Savage Fangs, The Faceless and The Helms. Varnia is the religious and trade hub, with Urdavah and Tommaso as major waypoints, and Chapter 9 (The Sage of the Desert) is the main-story chapter, also touching Demeniss.

records.name: The Abyss
records.summary: A sky layer above Pywel of floating puzzle islands, reached through Abyss Nexus and Gate points, and the source of Abyss Artifacts.
records.body: The Abyss is a separate map layer above the continent, not a ground region and with no ruling house in any source read here; it is reached through Abyss Nexus and Gate points. Its terrain is floating Sky Islands, each a self-contained puzzle, and Pearl Abyss calls it the cradle of providence. Abyss Artifacts collected there permanently raise Health, Stamina and Spirit and unlock skills, standing in for a traditional level system; the Library of Providence, its largest structure, holds lore on Pywel's making. The prologue and Chapter 1 use it for interludes ([[place:corridor-of-the-void]], [[place:axiom-archive]]); Chapter 12 climaxes here, and the epilogue returns for the forty Abyss Challenges' true ending.
